title: One Ratio, Two Formulas Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Vinegar is sour, glucose is sweet and formalin preserves lab specimens, yet all three carry their atoms in the same simple ratio, C : H : O = 1 : 2 : 1. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 1, Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry) we see why one compound can have two formulas.

You will see what an empirical formula (the simplest whole-number ratio) and a molecular formula (the exact count in one molecule) mean, using glucose, C6H12O6 = 6 x CH2O. On the molecule bench, benzene opens into six identical CH pieces, and two of those pieces join through three shared electron pairs to make acetylene, C2H2. Then we find a formula from nothing but percentages (mass % -> grams in 100 g -> moles -> divide by the smallest -> n), solve the NCERT example that gives CH2Cl and C2H4Cl2, see the exam trap of rounding 1 : 1.5, and finish with an original NEET pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 11 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:
0:00 Three substances, one ratio
0:30 Empirical vs molecular formula
1:08 Molecule bench: benzene splits into CH
1:53 Pause and think: benzene vs acetylene
2:07 Formula from percentages, step by step
3:12 NCERT worked example: CH2Cl to C2H4Cl2
4:05 Exam trap: never round 1 : 1.5
4:28 Practice question (NEET pattern)
5:15 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode: Chemical Equations and Stoichiometry. How much oxygen does a flame really use up?
